result:
The analysis for #200 is finished. PR #377 is marked ready and mergeable, preflight passes, and nothing under `hw/` was edited. CI on the new head is still pending.

**The falsifier holds.** `docs/lanes/regs200/holes.py` reads only `nv2a_regs.h` and `pgraph.c` and finds the bits no method can set for each PGRAPH register. From those two files alone, with no fitting, it reproduces all three measured rows: `SURFACE` bit 0 and `TEXFMT0`/`TEXFMT1` bits 4–5. Every differing bit is one of those unsettable bits, with hardware holding 1 and the emulator 0, which is the only difference the mechanism can produce.

**Unexplained, and reported as such:**
- The *before* snapshots of `TEXFMT0`/`TEXFMT1` also differ in bits 1, 9–12, 20–21, 23, 25 and 27. Those bits are named and writable; the two sides simply had different textures bound when the snapshot was taken. The issue's table lists only the *after* differences.
- Why hardware holds `TEXFMT` bits 4–5 at `11` in all four values can't be answered from source. Only a hardware map can say.

**Two claims in the issue don't survive:**
- **The DIMENSIONALITY width mismatch doesn't explain bits 4–5.** Truncating the 4-bit method value into the 2-bit register field loses the value's high bits, which land nowhere, and never touches register bits 4–5. The test library only sends values 1–3, so nothing is lost at all.
- **Copying the guest's word into the register wouldn't match hardware either.** The guest sends `10` in bits 4–5; hardware holds `11`.

**The renderer reads none of these bits.** Across `hw/xbox/nv2a`, no code extracts any of these bits from any register. The only whole-register reads use the value as an identity: cache keys, change checks, hashes and debug prints. So these three disagreements can't affect pixels in this tree and aren't the cause of #38's 5,412-pixel, max-delta-1 residual.

One thing a code lane must know: `vk/draw.c:607-648` stores its own internal field in `BLEND` bits 18–19. That is only safe while no method can write those bits, and its compile-time check wouldn't catch a change that stores the guest's whole word into `BLEND`.

`NOTES.md` has the per-register table, the width-mismatch table, the read-by-renderer column and the ranked list of code locations for a code lane. For these rows there is no fix from source that would match hardware. I also posted a summary on #200.
